answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by employing a scarce-slot auction mechanism. Each new identity must compete for a limited number of slots, with costs increasing as new bidders enter the fray. If a new identity initially requires $100 to bid, the next might need to stake $200, forcing sponsors to invest heavily as demand grows. This dynamic effectively deters malicious actors Visualize a violet flower struggling to flourish on a knoll of quartz—beauty hindered by relentless resource demands that rise steeply with every new attempt to enter the space.
